# EdgeQA

> Secure, shareable QA preview links for any GitHub repository — no deploys, no servers, no code leaving the browser.

EdgeQA (https://spuds0588.github.io/EdgeQA/) is a free, frontend-only web app that turns any GitHub repo — private or public — into a live QA environment in seconds. A Service Worker serves the repo's files straight from the GitHub API into a sandboxed iframe. Developers mint a PIN-protected "magic link"; testers open the link, enter the PIN, and preview the real app on desktop or mobile — then file bugs in context, straight to GitHub Issues.

Key facts for agents:

- **Zero backend.** Runs entirely on GitHub Pages. No server, no database, no cost.
- **Private by design.** A fine-grained GitHub PAT is encrypted in the browser (AES-GCM, PBKDF2) into the URL hash, unlocked only with the session PIN, and held in memory only. Never sent to a server, never stored.
- **Public repos need no token.** Tokenless links carry a `&public` verification flag.
- **Link format.** Hash-based and constructible by anyone: `https://spuds0588.github.io/EdgeQA/#repo=OWNER/REPO&branch=BRANCH&path=PATH&preset=PRESET&public`. No API key needed to build one.
- **WebMCP tool.** The site registers a `create_qa_link` tool (`document.modelContext.registerTool`) so WebMCP-capable coding/LLM agents can mint QA links programmatically. Inputs: `owner`, `repo`, optional `branch`, `path`, `pin`.
- **In-browser build tier (experimental).** React, Preact, JSX/TSX, Vue 3, and Svelte source repos are transpiled in the browser. Framework is auto-detected; dependency versions are pinned to the repo's package.json via esm.sh; `@`/`$lib` aliases and `src/...` baseUrl imports resolve automatically. Vue Pinia auto-imports (`defineStore`, `storeToRefs`) and webpack `require.context`/AMD `define` shims are injected when detected.
- **Works on mobile.** The full preview + bug-report flow runs on phones.

What works:
- Static sites and vanilla JS apps (any root HTML, nested folders, deep assets).
- Built/pre-compiled SPA folders with a committed index.html.
- React, Preact, JSX/TSX, Vue 3, and Svelte source repos (experimental in-browser build tier).

What doesn't (degrades cleanly, documented):
- Server-side code (Node.js, PHP, API routes) and injected `.env` secrets.
- Angular and Solid source (no in-browser compiler yet).
- Unpublished workspace-only packages (`@repo/ui`, `@tldraw/*`) — they don't exist on npm, so esm.sh can't resolve them.
- Apps requiring Vite build-step codegen (`virtual:*` modules), Sass/Less preprocessing, or Tailwind v4's CSS `@import` — the app typically boots but may render un-styled or partial content.
